title: Annotatio IV §.V open: Pauline true sentence endured through the Apostolic first age
pass_a_gloss: §. V. That the Pauline Mind and true Sentence concerning the Sacred Supper set out thus far — exactly congruent both with Christ’s Institution words and with their Antecedent Commentary handed down in John 6 — endured through the whole First age of the Christian era, i.e. the Apostolic, and was approved by the reckoning of all the Apostles and their Disciples (among whom Polycarp, John’s disciple, is numbered), may not absurdly be understood.
pass_b_english: §.V: the Pauline true Supper sentence — matching Institution and the John 6 antecedent commentary — lasted through the whole Apostolic first age.
All the Apostles and their disciples (Polycarp among them, John’s disciple) may fairly be read as approving it.
source_text: §. V. Expositam hactenus Paulinam de S. Cœna Mentem Sententiamque veram, Christi Verbis Institutionis æquè atque horum Commentario Antecedaneo, Joh. cap. 6. tradito, exactè congruam, totô æræ Christianæ seculô Primô, i. e. Apostolicô, perdurasse, eoque omnium Apostolorum horumque Discipulorum (quos inter Polycarpus, Johannis Discipulus, numeratur) probatam calculo fuisse, haud absurdè intelligi datur.
notes: §.V open: Pauline sentence through Apostolic age.
